issue.title: Toolbar does not hide while editing text on mobile
issue.body:
_From the tldraw product description's [bug triage](https://github.com/steveruizok/tldraw-product-description/blob/main/bug-triage.md) (B-50); read from the code at commit `c2c2eba669`, not yet confirmed in a browser unless a Status line says so._

**Where the user meets it**
Editing text on a phone.

**What happens / what was expected**
The UI computes a "hide the toolbar while editing" flag on iOS and Android (with a 150 ms delay on Android) and stamps it on the layout, but no stylesheet reads it, so the toolbar stays where it is. Expected: the toolbar hides, as the code intends.

**Reproduce**
needs a touch device. Double-click a shape to edit text; watch the toolbar.

**Why (from the code)**
`packages/tldraw/src/lib/ui/TldrawUi.tsx` lines 132–160 compute `hideToolbarWhileEditing` and line 195 sets `data-iseditinganything` on `.tlui-layout`; no selector in `packages/tldraw/src/lib/ui.css` matches it (the `.tl-canvas[data-iseditinganything]` rules in `tldraw.css` target a different element).

**Severity:** `medium`.

**Decision needed:** `fix`, or remove the dead flag.

**Raised by:** [toolbar](https://github.com/steveruizok/tldraw-product-description/blob/main/ui/toolbar.md#open-questions-and-verification), [editing text](https://github.com/steveruizok/tldraw-product-description/blob/main/tools/select/editing-text.md#open-questions-and-verification).

issue.title: Screen-reader announcements say "tool.group" and "0 of N"
issue.body:
_From the tldraw product description's [bug triage](https://github.com/steveruizok/tldraw-product-description/blob/main/bug-triage.md) (B-51); read from the code at commit `c2c2eba669`, not yet confirmed in a browser unless a Status line says so._

**Where the user meets it**
Selecting a group, or a shape inside a frame or group, with a screen reader running.

**What happens / what was expected**
A group is announced with the raw key "tool.group" because no translation exists for it; a nested shape is announced as "0 of N" because the index counts only top-level shapes. Expected: a real name and a real position.

**Reproduce**
1. Turn on a screen reader. 2. Group two shapes and select the group; then select a shape inside a frame.

**Why (from the code)**
`packages/tldraw/src/lib/ui/components/A11y.tsx` lines 111–131 use `msg(\`tool.${shape.type}\`)` and `getCurrentPageShapesInReadingOrder()`, which filters to page-level shapes (`Editor.ts` line 2327); `defaultTranslation.ts` has no `tool.group` key.

**Severity:** `medium`.

**Decision needed:** `fix`.

**Raised by:** [accessibility](https://github.com/steveruizok/tldraw-product-description/blob/main/cross-cutting/accessibility.md#edge-cases).

issue.title: Follow tooltip says "Following", Windows shortcuts mix Ctrl and ⇧, and the shortcuts preference only disables some keys
issue.body:
_From the tldraw product description's [bug triage](https://github.com/steveruizok/tldraw-product-description/blob/main/bug-triage.md) (B-59); read from the code at commit `c2c2eba669`, not yet confirmed in a browser unless a Status line says so._

**Where the user meets it**
The people menu's follow button; the shortcuts dialog on Windows; the keyboard-shortcuts preference.

**What happens / what was expected**
The follow button's tooltip says "Following" before the user follows anyone, because the `follow` and `following` strings are identical. On Windows the dialog renders `Ctrl+⇧+Z`, mixing a word and a glyph. With "Enable keyboard shortcuts" off, Delete stops working while Enter, Tab, and the arrows keep working, because Delete is a shortcut and the others are handled by the select tool. Expected: "Follow" / "Following"; "Ctrl+Shift+Z"; one rule for which keys the preference disables.

**Reproduce**
1. Open the people menu in a synced room and hover a follow button. 2. Open the shortcuts dialog on Windows. 3. Turn the preference off and press Delete on a selection.

**Why (from the code)**
`packages/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/useTranslation/defaultTranslation.ts` lines 376–377; `packages/tldraw/src/lib/ui/kbd-utils.ts` lines 18–50 always replace `shift+` with `⇧`; `useKeyboardShortcuts.ts` `areShortcutsDisabled` (lines 214–219) gates actions on the preference while `Idle.ts` handles Enter, Tab, and arrows itself.

**Severity:** `low`.

**Decision needed:** `fix`.

**Raised by:** [collaboration](https://github.com/steveruizok/tldraw-product-description/blob/main/cross-cutting/collaboration.md#open-questions-and-verification), [keyboard shortcuts](https://github.com/steveruizok/tldraw-product-description/blob/main/ui/keyboard-shortcuts.md#open-questions-and-verification), [accessibility](https://github.com/steveruizok/tldraw-product-description/blob/main/cross-cutting/accessibility.md#open-questions-and-verification).

+
+// Without a serializer, tiptap's `getText` treats a list, each of its items, and each item's
+// paragraph as separate blocks, so the block separator lands three times between items and the
+// markers are lost. This renders one `- ` / `1. ` line per item (nested lists indented) instead.
+//
+// `range` is the selection being serialized, in document positions: blocks outside it are
+// skipped, blocks straddling its edges are cut to it, and a line only gets its marker when the
+// selection begins at or before the line's first character.
+function renderListToText(
+	list: Node,
+	listPos: number,
+	range: Range,
+	textSerializers: Record<string, TextSerializer>,
+	indent = ''
+): string {
+	const isOrdered = list.type.name === 'orderedList'
+	const start: number = list.attrs.start ?? 1
+	const lines: string[] = []
+	list.forEach((item, itemOffset, index) => {
+		const marker = isOrdered ? `${start + index}. ` : '- '
+		const continuation = ' '.repeat(marker.length)
+		const itemPos = listPos + 1 + itemOffset
+		item.forEach((child, childOffset, childIndex) => {
+			const childPos = itemPos + 1 + childOffset
+			if (childPos >= range.to || childPos + child.nodeSize <= range.from) return
+			if (isListNode(child)) {
+				lines.push(renderListToText(child, childPos, range, textSerializers, indent + continuation))
+				return
+			}
+			const contentStart = childPos + 1
+			const prefix =
+				range.from <= contentStart ? indent + (childIndex === 0 ? marker : continuation) : ''
+			const text = getTextBetween(
+				child,
+				{
+					from: Math.max(0, range.from - contentStart),
+					to: Math.min(child.content.size, range.to - contentStart),
+				},
+				{ blockSeparator: '\n', textSerializers }

+ * A customizer for {@link isEqualWith}. Return `true` or `false` to decide equality for a pair of
+ * values yourself, or `undefined` to fall back to the default deep comparison for that pair. The
+ * customizer is invoked for the root values first and then for every nested pair.
+ *
+ * For nested pairs, `key` is the property name, array index or map key the values were found
+ * under, and `parent` / `otherParent` are the containers they came from. All three are `undefined`
+ * for the root pair, and `key` is also `undefined` when comparing set members or map keys.
+ *
+ * @public
+ */
+export type IsEqualCustomizer = (
+	a: unknown,
+	b: unknown,
+	key: PropertyKey | undefined,
+	parent: unknown,
+	otherParent: unknown
+) => boolean | undefined
+
+/**
+ * Deep equality comparison of two values.
+ *
+ * Compares primitives by value (`NaN` equals `NaN`), and recursively compares arrays, plain
+ * objects and class instances (own enumerable string keys), `Date`, `RegExp`, `Map`, `Set`,
+ * `ArrayBuffer` and typed arrays. Objects with different constructors (including null-prototype
+ * objects versus plain objects) are never equal, and symbol keys are ignored. Circular references
+ * are tolerated.
+ *
+ * @param a - The first value
+ * @param b - The second value
+ * @returns True if the values are deeply equal
+ *
+ * @example
+ * ```ts
+ * isEqual({ a: [1, { b: 2 }] }, { a: [1, { b: 2 }] }) // true
+ * isEqual(new Map([['x', 1]]), new Map([['x', 1]])) // true
+ * isEqual(NaN, NaN) // true
+ * isEqual({ a: 1 }, { a: 1, b: undefined }) // false
+ * ```
+ *
+ * @public
+ */
+export function isEqual(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
+	return baseIsEqual(a, b, undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined)
+}
+
+/**
+ * Deep equality comparison of two values with a customizer that can override the comparison for
+ * any pair of values. See {@link IsEqualCustomizer}.
+ *
+ * @param a - The first value
+ * @param b - The second value
+ * @param customizer - Decides equality for a pair, or returns `undefined` to use the default.
+ * Omitting it makes this the same as {@link isEqual}.
+ * @returns True if the values are deeply equal
+ *
+ * @example
+ * ```ts
+ * // Compare numbers with a tolerance, everything else structurally
+ * isEqualWith({ x: 0.1 + 0.2 }, { x: 0.3 }, (a, b) => {

+	return baseIsEqual(a, b, undefined, undefined, undefined, customizer, undefined)

+// means we're in a cycle; it is equal only if it's paired with the same partner as before (the
+// same rule lodash uses), which is also what stops the recursion.
+type Stack = Map<object, object>
+
+function baseIsEqual(
+	a: unknown,
+	b: unknown,
+	key: PropertyKey | undefined,
+	parent: unknown,
+	otherParent: unknown,
+	customizer: IsEqualCustomizer | undefined,
+	stack: Stack | undefined

+		const result = customizer(a, b, key, parent, otherParent)
+		if (result !== undefined) return result
+	}
+
+	if (a === b) return true
+	// NaN is the only value that is not equal to itself
+	if (a !== a && b !== b) return true
+
+	if (typeof a !== 'object' || typeof b !== 'object' || a === null || b === null) {
+		return false
+	}

+	stack ??= new Map()
+	const partner = stack.get(a)
+	if (partner !== undefined) return partner === b
+
+	stack.set(a, b)
+	try {
+		return compareObjects(a, b, customizer, stack)
+	} finally {
+		stack.delete(a)
+	}

+function compareObjects(

+	b: object,
+	customizer: IsEqualCustomizer | undefined,

+		case '[object ArrayBuffer]':

+	if (a instanceof DataView) {

+			new Uint8Array(other.buffer, other.byteOffset, other.byteLength)

+			a as unknown as ArrayLike<unknown>,
+			b as unknown as ArrayLike<unknown>,
+			customizer,
+			stack
+		)

+	if (a.constructor !== b.constructor) return false

+	const keysA = Object.keys(a)

+		if (!baseIsEqual((a as any)[key], (b as any)[key], key, a, b, customizer, stack)) return false
+	}
+	return true
+}
+
+function compareArrays(
+	a: ArrayLike<unknown>,
+	b: ArrayLike<unknown>,
+	customizer: IsEqualCustomizer | undefined,

comment.body: Fixed in d758314923. With a customizer, a primitive set member or map key that has no exact match now falls back to the deep search, so the customizer gets to decide (e.g. isEqualAllowingForFloatingPointErrors on Sets of nearly-equal numbers). Without a customizer, the identity-only fast path is unchanged. Tests added.

**Progress counter can read past the total.** Failed files are counted in `++uploadedFiles + 1`. On the last iteration the progress toast briefly says 'Uploading 4 of 3 .tldr files…'. The off-by-one was already there, but it's now easier to see because failing files no longer stop the loop.

**`onUploadError` now also fires after partial success.** It used to mean the import failed and nothing more would happen. Now it can run after `onFirstFileUploaded` has already navigated to a new file. Current callers are fine (`importFromUrl` passes a single file), but the callback no longer has one clear meaning. Consider documenting it on the opts type, or passing the failed and created counts.

**Only parse errors get a reason; others say nothing.** The description compares against the magic string `'could not parse file'`, which is duplicated from `uploadTldrFile`. Any other failure (an upload `fetch` throwing, a `createFile` rejection) gets a title with no description, so the user can't tell a bad file from a transient failure that is worth retrying. Consider a shared constant or typed error, plus a generic 'try again' description for the other cases.

**One sticky toast per failed file.** Every failure adds its own `keepOpen: true` error toast. If 20 of 25 dropped files are invalid, the user has to dismiss 20 toasts. A failure from `createFile` also shows two toasts per file (createFile's own plus this one). Consider collecting the failed names and showing one summary toast after the loop, next to the existing success toast.

**Aborting skips `onUploadError`, so `importFromUrl` can hang.** Before this change a failure always called `onUploadError`. Now the aborted path returns with no callback. `importFromUrl` wraps this call in a Promise that resolves only from `onFirstFileUploaded`/`onUploadError`, so if the app is disposed mid-import the promise never settles. The same return also skips `clearTimeout(uploadingToastTimeout)`, the removal of the progress toast and `didFinishUploading`. Suggest calling `onUploadError?.()` before returning.

issue.title: Importing several .tldr files stops at the first failure with a generic error
issue.body:
When you import several .tldr files at once and one of them fails (for example, it can't be parsed), the import stops at that file. Files before it are created, files after it are silently skipped, and the only feedback is a generic "unknown error" toast that doesn't say which file failed.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On tldraw.com, signed in, select three .tldr files where the second is invalid (for example, a text file renamed to `.tldr`).
2. Drop them onto the app, or import them from the main menu.

## Expected

The valid files are imported, and the error names the file that couldn't be imported.

## Actual

The first file is created and opened. The second shows a generic unknown-error toast, and the third is never imported.

issue.title: Style dropdowns and the toolbar overflow stay open after open menus are cleared
issue.body:
The style panel dropdowns and the toolbar overflow popover keep their own `isOpen` state alongside the global menu registry. Calling `editor.menus.clearOpenMenus()` (or anything else that clears the registry) removes them from the registry but leaves them visibly open. While they stay open, `editor.menus.hasAnyOpenMenus()` reports `false`, so keyboard shortcuts start firing again.

## Steps to reproduce

issue.title: Hard-deleting a legacy room leaves its document in durable object storage
issue.body:
Hard-deleting a legacy (non-app) room through the admin `hard_delete_file` route removes its R2 snapshot and history but leaves the full document in the room durable object's SQLite storage. The app-file delete path explicitly wipes durable object storage ("so we don't keep the data around"); the legacy path doesn't, so a "hard deleted" legacy board's contents are still kept in Cloudflare storage indefinitely.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a legacy room (`/r/<slug>`) so its durable object loads the document into SQLite.
2. Hard-delete it with `POST /app/admin/hard_delete_file/<slug>`.
3. Inspect the room durable object's storage.

## Expected

Like an app-file delete, the durable object's SQLite tables are dropped (keeping only what's needed to keep the room marked deleted).

## Actual

R2 objects and history are deleted and `documentInfo` is marked `deleted`, but the `SQLiteSyncStorage` tables with every record in the room are left in place, and the in-memory `_storage` handle stays cached. The data is no longer served, since the deleted guards block reads, but it's never removed.

## Where

- [`__admin__hardDeleteIfLegacy`](https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/apps/dotcom/sync-worker/src/TLFileDurableObject.ts#L3632-L3659) closes sockets, nulls `_room` and deletes the R2 keys, but never calls `ctx.storage.deleteAll()` or clears `_storage`.
- Compare [`appFileRecordDidDelete`](https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/apps/dotcom/sync-worker/src/TLFileDurableObject.ts#L3383-L3449), which clears `_storage` and ends with `deleteAlarm()` + `deleteAll()`.

Possible direction: clear the durable object's storage the same way the app delete path does, then re-write the `deleted` `documentInfo` so the room stays terminal.

issue.title: TldrawImage leaks its temporary editor and container element

labels.name: repo-3bfec0a7
labels.description: Improve performance of an existing feature

issue.body:
`TldrawImage` creates a temporary `Editor` and a hidden container `div` each time its render effect runs, but only disposes the editor when the export finishes successfully. If the effect re-runs before the export resolves, or the export returns nothing, the editor is never disposed. Its container `div` is never removed in any case, so they pile up inside the component.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Render `<TldrawImage snapshot={...} bounds={new Box(...)} />` with a prop that changes identity on each render (for example an inline `bounds` or `options` object), or change props quickly while an export is in flight.
2. Inspect the component's container in devtools, or take a heap snapshot.

## Expected

Each run of the effect cleans up its editor and its temporary element when it is cancelled or finishes.

## Actual

Cancelled runs leave an undisposed `Editor` subscribed to the store, and every run leaves an empty `div` appended to the container.

## Where

- https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/packages/tldraw/src/lib/TldrawImage.tsx#L150-L201 — `editor.dispose()` (L193) runs only after a successful, non-cancelled `toImage`; the cleanup (L198-L200) only sets `isCancelled`, and `tempElm` (appended at L158) is never removed.

Possible direction: dispose the editor and remove `tempElm` in the effect cleanup and on every exit path of `setSvg`.

issue.title: A failed translation fetch causes an unhandled rejection and keeps the previous language
issue.body:
If the translation file for a locale fails to load (network error, 404, or a non-JSON response from a misconfigured `assetUrls.translations`), `TldrawUiTranslationProvider` leaves the promise rejection unhandled. The UI also stays in whatever language was loaded before, rather than falling back to English. On a locale switch, the UI keeps showing the previous language's strings, with the new locale's overrides layered on top.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Render `<Tldraw />` with `assetUrls.translations.fr` pointing to a URL that 404s (or block the request in devtools).
2. Switch the user's locale to French.

## Expected

The failure is handled (logged), and the UI falls back to English for the missing catalog.

## Actual

An `Unhandled promise rejection` appears in the console, and the previous language stays loaded.

## Where

- https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/packages/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/useTranslation/translations.ts#L46-L47 — `fetch` and `res.json()` are awaited without a `res.ok` check or `try`/`catch`.
- https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/packages/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/useTranslation/useTranslation.tsx#L85-L98 — `loadTranslation()` is called without a `.catch`, so `setLoaded` never runs on failure.

issue.title: Undoing a file drop mid-upload leaves an orphaned asset in the document
issue.body:
When files are dropped or pasted onto the canvas, the uploads start before the shapes are created and always write their result back with `updateAssets` when they finish. If shape creation is refused (the page is at its max shapes) or the drop is undone before the upload completes, the finished upload still writes a full asset record into the store. That leaves an orphaned asset that no shape references. Because `updateAssets` merges onto a missing record, it effectively creates the asset.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Drop a large image or video onto the canvas over a slow connection (throttle the network in devtools).
2. Press Undo before the upload finishes.
3. Wait for the upload to complete, then inspect `editor.getAssets()`.

(Or: fill a page to `maxShapesPerPage` and drop a file.)

## Expected

No asset record remains once its shape is gone or was never created, and the uploaded file is not attached to the document.

## Actual

The uploaded asset is added to the document with no shape referencing it.

## Where

- https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/packages/tldraw/src/lib/defaultExternalContentHandlers.ts#L507-L533 — uploads start in `Promise.allSettled` before `createShapesForAssets` and call `updateAssets` unconditionally on success.
- https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/packages/tldraw/src/lib/defaultExternalContentHandlers.ts#L826-L838 — `createShapesForAssets` silently creates neither assets nor shapes when `canCreateShapes` fails.
- https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/packages/editor/src/lib/editor/Editor.ts#L10019-L10045 — the paste path has the same pattern.
- https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/packages/editor/src/lib/editor/Editor.ts#L5243-L5258 — `updateAssets` spreads the partial over `store.get(id)!`, which re-creates a removed record.

Possible direction: only write the uploaded asset back if the asset still exists in the store.

issue.title: Scribble session with no scribbles is removed before it is stopped
issue.body:
A scribble session that has no visible scribbles is reaped on the next tick even though it was never stopped. Calling `editor.scribbles.addScribbleToSession()` with that session id afterwards throws `Session <id> not found`, which crashes a custom tool that starts its session ahead of its first stroke or reuses a session across strokes.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a custom tool's `onEnter`, call `const id = editor.scribbles.startSession()`.
2. Let a frame pass.
3. On the next pointer down, call `editor.scribbles.addScribbleToSession(id, { color: 'accent' })`.

The same happens with an `individual`-fade session that is reused across strokes: once every scribble in it has faded out, the session is removed even though `stopSession` was never called.

## Expected

A session stays active until `stopSession`, `clearSession` or its idle timeout ends it, so it can be created before its first scribble and reused.

## Actual

The session is marked `complete` and deleted on the next tick, and `addScribbleToSession` throws `Session <id> not found`.

## Where

- [ScribbleManager.ts#L426-L430](https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/packages/editor/src/lib/editor/managers/ScribbleManager/ScribbleManager.ts#L426-L430): `tickSession` marks a session complete when it has no content and `session.items.length === 0`, regardless of whether it is still `active`; `tick` then deletes it ([L376-L382](https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/packages/editor/src/lib/editor/managers/ScribbleManager/ScribbleManager.ts#L376-L382)).
- [ScribbleManager.ts#L116-L117](https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/packages/editor/src/lib/editor/managers/ScribbleManager/ScribbleManager.ts#L116-L117): `addScribbleToSession` throws for a missing session.
- The built-in laser tool is not affected because it starts the session and adds its first scribble in the same call, and checks `isSessionActive` first.

issue.title: Pattern fills keep the old color after switching themes
issue.body:
The on-canvas pattern fill is generated from the current theme's `solid` colors, but the generator reads the theme outside React's dependency tracking. Switching themes at runtime with `editor.setCurrentTheme` or `editor.updateThemes` leaves pattern-filled shapes drawn in the previous theme's color until the device pixel ratio or zoom steps change, or the editor remounts.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Register two themes whose `colors.light.solid` (or `colors.dark.solid`) differ.
2. Draw a shape with the pattern fill.
3. Call `editor.setCurrentTheme` to switch to the other theme.

## Expected

The hatch pattern regenerates in the new theme's color.

## Actual

The pattern keeps the old theme's color.

## Where

- https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw/blob/616a7c49576f139dc5d091e0621cb589c48a80d8/packages/tldraw/src/lib/shapes/shared/defaultStyleDefs.tsx#L219-L261 — `usePattern` calls `editor.getCurrentTheme()` inside a `useEffect` whose dependencies are only `[dpr, maxEffectiveZoom, editor]`, so a theme change never re-runs it.
